461-program-description: B.A. & Sc. only: cognition in humans and machines, to understand intelligence and thought, learning and intelligent devices. At least 21 credits each in Arts and Science with your minor.
465-computer-science: In the B.A. & Sc., the Computer Science minor and major and the Software Engineering major count as Science.
465-about-computer-science: The theory and practice of computing systems, built on algorithms and programming. Areas include data structures, languages, theory, software engineering, architecture, networks, operating systems, databases, AI, vision, graphics, robotics and computational biology. It feeds into biology, physics, business, music and neuroscience.
Strong job prospects in development, consulting, research and project management; be ready to learn your application domain.

Science offers Major (Games and AI options), Honours, Liberal and Minor in CS, and Major, Honours and Liberal in Software Engineering. Arts and B.A. & Sc. have concentrations. Engineering students can take electives or a minor (p. 803).
Most programs share basic courses, so you can decide later. Interactive teaching, research chances, some graduate courses for seniors, and undergraduate labs in the Trottier Building. See an adviser.
465-internship-opportunities: Internship Year in Science: 8, 12 or 16 months, shown on your transcript and program name. Industrial Practicum: four months, usually from May, 0-credit pass/fail; two of them add "internship" to the program name.
465-research-opportunities: Summer awards such as NSERC USRA, assistantships and lab volunteering. Project courses COMP 396, 400 and 401. Broad research may qualify you for the Dean's list (p. 67).
466-admissions: Have MATH 140 (or 150), 141 (or 151) and 133 or CEGEP equivalents, averaging at least B-. No computing background needed; start with COMP 202, 204 or 208. COMP 202 early lets you take advanced courses sooner.
466-location: McConnell Engineering Building, Room 318, 3480 University St. Advising: Room 320.
468-program-description: Methods for designing complex software. Finish MATH 133, 140 and 141 or equivalents first. Doesn't lead to Professional Engineer certification.
468-required-courses-30-credits: With programming knowledge, replace COMP 202 with a complementary.
469-about-earth-and-planetary-sciences: The solid Earth, hydrosphere, other terrestrial planets and exoplanets, using chemistry, physics and math, plus geomicrobiology and the search for early and alien life.
16 professors, 2 lecturers, about 70 graduate and 20–30 undergraduates, so small friendly classes.
Careers in resource exploration, environmental and geotechnical consulting, summer jobs with industry and government, and planetary science research.
469-undergraduate-studies: A strong base in physical sciences with flexibility for industry, teaching or research.

B.Sc. Major Geology suits those seeking a professional geoscientist licence. Honours in Planetary Sciences adds math and physics. Liberal is less specialized. Also a joint Major in Physics and Geophysics and Earth System Science.
Minor in Geology for other departments, assuming general chemistry and foundation science. Minor in Geochemistry for chemistry majors. B.A. students can specialize here in Science for Arts.
469-location: Frank Dawson Adams Building, 3450 University St., Room 238. Director of Undergraduate Studies: Professor Jeanne Paquette, Room 310.
470-program-description: Exposure to Earth Sciences for students from other departments.
470-complementary-courses-12-credits: 3 from the first list and 9 from the second, or other EPSC at 300+ with permission.
499-environment: Bieler's programs for B.A. & Sc. students.
499-location: Downtown: 3534 University St. Macdonald: Rowles House, 21,111 Lakeshore Rd.
499-program-description: Why environmental problems are complex and contested: global climate, socio-economic challenges, geological and biological change, and ethics and culture.
499-complementary-courses-18-credits: All outside your major's field and at 200+. 12 credits of core courses, then environment-related ones.
500-natural-sciences-and-technology: 0–3 credits. One each of: LSCI 230 or MIMM 211; ENVB 529 or GEOG 201; BREE 217, CIVE 323 or GEOG 322; BIOL 308 or ENVB 305; BIOL 465 or WILD 421; COMP 202 or 204; EPSC 201 or 233.
501-complementary-courses-18-credits: All outside your major's field and at 200+. 12 core ENVR credits, Section 001 downtown or 051 at Macdonald. 6 related credits with approval, at least 3 in social sciences.
501-suggested-course-list: Two themes: Social Sciences and Policy, and Natural Sciences and Technology. Not exhaustive; others with the Adviser's permission. Most 300+ have prerequisites, and some are restricted.
501-location-note: Courses run on both campuses; check where each is.
502-natural-sciences-and-technology: One each of: LSCI 230 or MIMM 211; ENVB 529 or GEOG 201; BREE 217, CIVE 323 or GEOG 322; BIOL 308 or ENVB 305; BIOL 465 or WILD 421; COMP 202 or 204; EPSC 201 or 233.
503-program-description: Environmental problems facing society, flexibly: broad training or depth in your interests.
503-program-requirements: At most 21 at 200, at least 12 at 400+. At least 21 credits each in Arts and Science with your minor; ENVR splits between both. Courses run on both campuses.
504-areas: 30 credits from at least three Areas, at least 6 at 400+.
504-area-4-hydrology-and-water-resources: One of GEOG 322, BREE 217 or CIVE 323; EPSC 522 or GEOG 522.
505-program-description: For those in the Interfaculty Program. Apply in March of U2 with program GPA 3.3. B or higher in ENVR 495, CGPA 3.0 and program GPA 3.3 at graduation. 21 credits each in Arts and Science with your minor.
54 credits plus 6 Honours credits. Present at an Honours Symposium and submit your report.
506-honours-required-courses-6-credits: ENVR 495D1 and D2 over consecutive terms, or N1 and N2 otherwise.
507-field-study: See Field Study Programs and the Field Studies Adviser.
507-program-description: 15 credits of a field semester (Africa, Barbados, BITS, Arctic or Panama) plus 3 chosen with an adviser. It can serve as the B.Sc. Liberal breadth component. Semesters aren't degrees; credits count with advisers' permission.
507-africa-field-study-semester-15-credi: A term in East Africa through the Canadian Field Study in Africa Program, on conservation, culture change and sustainable development, in settings from highlands and desert to lakes, coast and cities.
507-africa-field-study-semester-required: One Research in Society and Development course and one Research in Ecology and Development course.
507-barbados-field-study-semester-15-cre: With the University of the West Indies, at Bellairs: sustainability science in the Caribbean, field research, and an applied project with local partners.
508-barbados-interdisciplinary-tropical-: Each summer: two orientation sessions, then three 3-credit and one 6-credit project courses at Bellairs, on sustainable food, nutrition and energy on a tourism-based island. Builds planning and management skills. Open to senior undergraduates across McGill.
508-panama-field-study-semester-15-credi: With the Smithsonian: team research with Panamanian institutions on practical environmental problems, a short transition and 13 weeks in Panama, with field trips.
508-panama-field-study-semester-compleme: 6 credits, changing yearly; register for those offered in your Winter.
508-minor-field-studies-complementary-co: After a field semester, choose 3 credits with your adviser and ask for it to be added to your record.
509-about-gender-sexuality-feminist-and-: Interdisciplinary study of gender, sexuality and feminism through social justice, including critical race, disability and Indigenous studies.
516-location: Burnside Hall, Floors 3–7, 805 Sherbrooke St. W. Administrative Office: Room 305.
519-program-description-2: An overview for Science students, expandable into the B.Sc. Major, with no overlap with other programs.
520-program-description-2: B.A. & Sc. only: a planned sequence for specialization.
536-available-programs: Includes Quebec Studies and Community-Engaged Learning (p. 541).
